article.headline: GTA 6 Clings to 30 FPS on PS5 Pro as Upgrades Revealed
article.summary: Rockstar Games confirmed GTA 6 will maintain 30 frames per second on all consoles when it launches on November 19.
article.body:
Rockstar Games has confirmed that Grand Theft Auto VI will run at 30 frames per second on the PlayStation 5 Pro, silencing rumors that the enhanced console would push the frame rate higher to 40 or 60 frames per second. Instead of higher frame rates, the additional power of the PS5 Pro will be dedicated to enhanced visual fidelity, including PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR) upscaling for improved clarity and exclusive ray-traced shadows. 

For players, this news clarifies the performance expectations for the game's launch. By focusing the console's resources on image quality and environmental density rather than performance speed, Rockstar aims to maintain the visual fidelity of the world of Leonida across the current generation of hardware. The developer noted that the game is designed to push all consoles to their absolute limits to bring the expansive setting to life.

According to Digital Foundry, the PS5 family remains the lead platform for the release, featuring high-quality haptic feedback via the DualSense controller and improved spatial audio rendering. Meanwhile, The Verge reports that Microsoft has secured rights to stream the game via Xbox Cloud Gaming, exclusively for Xbox One and Xbox Series consoles. This move allows those on older Xbox One hardware to experience the game through cloud streaming, which will utilize Xbox Series S graphics settings.

Game pre-loads are currently underway for those ready to play as soon as the title officially launches. While cloud streaming is currently limited to Xbox consoles, Rockstar has confirmed that the game will also support Remote Play on both PlayStation and Xbox devices.

article.headline: Singaporeans Secure Final Assurance Package Cash Payouts of Up To $250
article.summary: Approximately 3 million Singaporean adults will receive final Assurance Package cash payouts ranging from $100 to $250 starting December 8.
article.body:
Over a five-year span ending in 2026, eligible Singaporeans will have collected a total of up to $2,250 in cash benefits through the government’s comprehensive support scheme. This December’s distribution marks the final installment of the enhanced Assurance Package, an initiative originally introduced to help households navigate rising living costs and the impact of the goods and services tax rate increases.

The Ministry of Finance confirmed that this disbursement serves as the final round of support under the program, which was bolstered by a $3 billion top-up during the 2023 budget. With total funding reaching $9.6 billion, the package has provided sustained assistance to lower- and middle-income families across the nation since 2022.

Individual payouts are determined by assessable income and property ownership status. Citizens owning no more than one property with an annual income of $39,000 or below qualify for the maximum $250 payment. Those with incomes between $39,001 and $100,000 will receive $150, while individuals earning above $100,000 or owning multiple properties are set to receive $100. Eligibility applies to all Singaporeans aged 21 and older as of 2027.

Recipients can verify their status via the official govbenefits.gov.sg portal using Singpass credentials. Notifications will be dispatched via SMS from the official gov.sg Sender ID, while those without registered mobile numbers will receive physical letters. To ensure an earlier arrival on December 8, eligible recipients must link their NRIC to PayNow by November 24. Those opting for GIRO payments must submit their banking details by November 30 to receive funds by December 17.

article.headline: DSWD Distributes P189 Million to Farmers Devastated by El Niño Drought Conditions
article.summary: The Department of Social Welfare and Development has released over P189 million in emergency cash and food packs to support drought-stricken farmers as of November 7.
article.body:
The scale of the crisis facing the agricultural sector is evident in the numbers: over 191,000 families across six regions have been directly impacted by the drought. While the national farm output dropped by 5 percent in the third quarter, the rice harvest alone suffered a 17.8 percent decline, leaving farmers in a precarious financial position. According to DSWD Assistant Secretary Irene Dumlao, some agricultural workers have halted planting entirely, fearing that another failed harvest would erase all investments in labor and seeds.

This humanitarian assistance is a critical lifeline for families whose crops have been decimated. By prioritizing those identified by local governments as most severely affected, the agency aims to mitigate the immediate impact of the weather phenomenon. The support package combines emergency cash transfers with essential family food packs, providing basic sustenance to communities from the Cagayan Valley to the Bicol region.

Data from the DSWD reveals that the agency has provided more than P141 million specifically to corn and rice farmers in Isabela and Cagayan. In Camarines Norte, more than P31 million was recently disbursed to 1,967 beneficiaries in Capalonga and 1,002 in Paracale. These figures are expected to climb as additional field reports are processed, particularly as national rice stocks have thinned by 8.3 percent and government buffers have plummeted by 38 percent.

Further cash transfers are slated for additional towns in Camarines Norte throughout this week and next. Recipients in these upcoming rounds are scheduled to receive P10,000 each. As the weather bureau warns that as many as 68 provinces could face drought conditions by February, the DSWD continues to monitor the situation across the six affected regions.

article.headline: England mandates total phone ban as pupils face strict September 2027 rules
article.summary: The government is strengthening guidance to ensure truly phone-free school days by prohibiting students from keeping mobile devices in their bags or pockets.
article.body:
Starting in September 2027, pupils in England will no longer be permitted to keep mobile phones in their bags or pockets throughout the school day. While current policies often rely on 'not seen, not heard' rules, the updated government guidance aims to eliminate digital distractions entirely. Education Secretary Lucy Powell stated the objective is to ensure that schools remain environments for learning and friendship rather than scrolling, noting that phone access risks pulling children away from their studies and social interactions.

This shift to 'truly phone-free' schools is intended to foster a whole-school culture change. Proponents argue that restricting access improves focus in lessons and encourages face-to-face socialization. Karl Harrison, head teacher at Burnage Academy for Boys, reported that investing in systems like metal detectors and secure pouches has already resulted in higher grades and increased student interaction at his school.

Schools will retain flexibility in how they enforce these requirements, with potential methods including the use of locked storage, collection at the start of the day, or outright prohibitions on devices being brought to school sites. The Department for Education acknowledges that some institutions have already successfully implemented such measures.

However, leadership unions have raised concerns regarding the implementation of these more robust rules. Both the NAHT and the Association of School and College Leaders have warned that schools will struggle to manage these mandates without additional government funding. While the updated guidance offers clearer expectations for head teachers, union representatives emphasized that schools cannot simply make the logistical challenge of mobile phones disappear without the necessary financial support.

article.headline: Hamilton rain washout forces Black Caps into desperate fight for series draw
article.summary: Heavy rain at Seddon Park abandoned the third ODI between New Zealand and India, leaving the hosts trailing 2-0 in the series.
article.body:
Not a single ball was bowled in Hamilton as persistent weather forced officials to abandon the third ODI of the series. The washout effectively ended New Zealand’s hopes of an ODI series victory against India, leaving the Black Caps unable to win the remaining two matches after already falling 2-0 behind following losses in Auckland and Wellington. The team now faces the prospect of their first home ODI series defeat since 2019.

This result is significant for the Black Caps, who have successfully defended their home turf by winning 11 consecutive ODI series over the last five years. For local fans who turned out for the sellout event, the abandonment denied any chance of a 40-overs-per-side contest. The loss of points and momentum comes at a difficult time as the squad prepares for upcoming test matches.

The challenge for New Zealand deepens as they enter games four and five without several key starters. Players including Tom Latham, Daryl Mitchell, Glenn Phillips, Henry Nicholls, and Nathan Smith are set to depart the ODI group to begin preparations for the test series in Wellington. Additionally, the side faces setbacks with players like Lockie Ferguson withdrawn due to injury, requiring a roster shuffle that brings in reinforcements like Finn Allen and Nick Kelly.

With only two games remaining, New Zealand must secure wins at Bay Oval to avoid a series loss. Both upcoming fixtures will test the depth of the squad as they look to salvage a 2-2 draw.

article.headline: Troy Aikman jokes about needing loan during ESPN contract standoff with network
article.summary: Analyst Troy Aikman quipped about his finances on air while calling the Bills' 23-6 victory over the Vikings amid stalled contract extension talks.
article.body:
During Monday's broadcast of the Buffalo Bills' dominant 23-6 win over the Minnesota Vikings, lead analyst Troy Aikman used an observation of Justin Jefferson’s diamond chains to highlight his own precarious contract status. Observing the jewelry, Aikman remarked, "I'm guessing that's insured. I cannot imagine wearing that on a football field. Can't imagine wearing it, period," before adding, "I might buy something similar if somebody would loan me some money." The comment caught the attention of viewers and former quarterback Kurt Benkert, who described the remark as a dig at his booth partner, Joe Buck, who recently secured a six-year, $108 million extension with ESPN.

This tension arrives as ESPN has paused negotiations with Aikman, whose camp reportedly sought a market-resetting extension near $30 million per year. While the duo has worked together since 2002, the current stalemate regarding Aikman’s future has created friction, according to reports. Aikman’s current contract is set to expire in March, leaving the long-running broadcast partnership with an uncertain future beyond the current season.

On the field, the broadcast focused on Minnesota's struggling offense, which Aikman described as difficult to fix. The Vikings benched quarterback Carson Wentz late in the game after he produced only 81 passing yards and three turnovers. The win moved Buffalo to 7-1 on the season as they prepare for a matchup against the New York Jets, while the 6-2 Vikings look to address their quarterback situation ahead of a Week 10 game against the Green Bay Packers.

Criminal stars Charlie Hunnam, Adria Arjona, Luke Evans, Emilia Clarke, Richard Jenkins, Kadeem Hardison, Gus Halper, John Hawkes, and Logan Browning. The recurring and guest cast includes Michael Mando, Garrett Hedlund, Patrick J. And when Ricky's older brother Tracy (Luke Evans) returns home from the Army, their tragic family history comes home with him. Drawn into their orbit are Greta (Adria Arjona), a sharp-tongued car thief from Leo’s past, and Mallory (Emilia Clarke), Ricky's girlfriend, who fears what he'll do to get by. Gunfights, heists, and tragic romance are the order of the day, but will anyone make it out alive?Criminal is based on the graphic novels by Ed Brubaker and Sean Phillips, and executive produced by Brubaker, Phillips, Philipp A.
